result.rationale: The Watch band is defensible, but it is right for partly the wrong reasons and is more fragile than the score implies. The entire news contribution (weighted 13.7) comes from one headline-only article, GN-1caacc272320; payment alone contributes weighted 11.7, which sits below the Watch threshold of 20, so the band depends wholly on that single news item holding its severity 2. What actually sustains a Watch posture is the payment trajectory — resolution times lengthening from 5 to 9 to 18 days with the current item still open and the review flagged "deteriorating" — which the formula only sees as a point-in-time 18 DPD and therefore under-weights. I agree with Watch, but the underwriter should treat the payment trend, not the news item, as the load-bearing evidence.

concerns.issue: Sole driver of the news score (decayed 39.25, weighted 13.7) and therefore of the Watch band, yet the retrieved article contains no body text beyond its headline. The severity 2 rests on a 3.5% share price decline, which is a market reaction rather than a credit event, and it is filed under category 'profit_warning' although nothing in the evidence shows a company-issued guidance warning. A single unverifiable headline should not carry a band on its own, particularly when payment weighted 11.7 falls below the Watch threshold of 20 without it.

Reuters, published 2026-11-12 (one day before GN-1caacc272320), reports the same Q2 results as a narrowed quarterly loss on higher per-user revenue and was scored severity 0, base 0.0. Two opposing readings of one event sit in the evidence set and the scorer took only the max-severity one. This item is also headline-only, so neither can be reconciled against the underlying figures; the conflict is unresolved on the record.

The payment_review trend (5 days late, then 9, then currently 18 and still open, with notifications rising from 1 to 2 in the 180-day window) is the strongest credit signal here, but the formula ingests only the point-in-time 18 DPD as raw 18.0. The deterioration itself is unscored, so the payment leg is understated just as the news leg is overstated.

Internal inconsistency in the overdue amount: the notification data records owed as INR 40,000,000, while the payment_review describes the open overdue invoice as INR 9.0M with total exposure around 40M against a INR 120M limit. The 'owed' field appears to carry exposure rather than the past-due amount, which materially changes how the severity of the single open item reads.

All overdue notifications originate from the single policy TCI-SCF-2026-0001, as the review itself notes. Payment conduct outside this one facility is unobserved, so neither the deteriorating read nor a benign read can be generalised to the buyer's wider behaviour.
